title: Preregistered Paired Evaluation of a Deterministic Verifier Pipeline for LLM‑Generated Network Configuration Changes — Non‑informative Testability Failure
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment (cand-2026-01-prereg-v1) that tested whether deterministic verifier augmentation (generate → deterministic_netops_validator_v5 → optional repair) reduces the rate of verifier‑detected unsafe intent→configuration proposals from a hosted LLM on synthetic NetOps tasks. Design: N=200 preregistered intent→configuration tasks in a paired design comparing (a) baseline LLM‑only and (b) guarded pipeline (gpt-5-mini + deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (one shared LLM call per task) producing model_calls_used = 200. Observed (adversarial cluster): baseline SAFE = 200/200; guarded SAFE = 200/200 (paired contingency n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0). Estimated paired SAFE‑rate difference = 0.0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Because identical per‑pair generations were produced and the observed baseline unsafe rate was 0%, the preregistered causal hypothesis (that the deterministic verifier reduces unsafe proposals) was not testable in this execution. We publish the complete preregistered run and artifacts, provide an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of the testability failure, and give concrete, artifact‑supported recommendations (independent per‑arm generation budgeting, adversarial calibration, and exploratory ROC reserves) for informative repeats. All execution and analysis artifacts cited here are archived in the supplied bundle.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) are being applied to NetOps tasks (intent translation, configuration synthesis, and limited remediation) because they can reduce operator effort and speed routine changes. However, misordered or incorrect device changes risk outages and security exposures. A common mitigation architecture is tool‑augmentation: pair an LLM generator with deterministic validators, sandboxed simulators, or constrained executors in a generate–validate–repair pipeline so that proposed changes are checked before execution. Prior work documents both promise and safety concerns for agentic NetOps and advocates workflow‑centred, replayable evaluations with sandboxed validation (Bilal et al., 2026; Ferrag et al., 2026; Zhang et al., 2025).
sections.related_work: Surveys and prototype reports show growing interest in LLM‑assisted NetOps and emphasize evaluation sensitivity to task design, validator fidelity, and sampling semantics (Bilal et al., 2026; Liu et al., 2024). Tool‑augmentation patterns (generate–validate–refine or divide–verify–refine) have been shown to reduce constraint violations on curated tasks when the external verifier faithfully encodes domain constraints; however, effect sizes depend strongly on verifier completeness and how candidates are sampled and repaired (Zhang & Tang, 2025; Gao et al., 2023). Work on guardrails and schema‑based interfaces stresses operational trade‑offs: stricter validators may reduce unsafe acceptances but increase false refusals and operator workload, motivating ROC‑style diagnostics and adversarial calibration in evaluation design (Yadav, 2026; Ando, 2026). Our study aligns with these methodological recommendations by using deterministic task generation, preregistration, sandboxed deterministic validation, and archived validator traces to enable reproducible diagnosis.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as cand-2026-01-prereg-v1. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on binary SAFE indicators from a deterministic sandbox validator. Confirmatory test: exact two‑sided McNemar (paired_binary_analysis_v1); paired bootstrap CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). The preregistration specified N=200 paired tasks, power assumptions expecting a baseline unsafe rate ≈10–15%, and two permitted generation semantics: independent per‑arm generation (two independent LLM draws per task) or shared_initial_candidate (one shared LLM draw per task scored by both arms).

Task generation, pipelines, and scoring. A deterministic generator produced 200 synthetic intent→configuration tasks constrained to single‑AS, multi‑device topologies and limited fields (admin, mtu, vlan). Baseline pipeline: accept the LLM candidate and score post hoc with deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Guarded pipeline: validate the same candidate in a deterministic sandbox with deterministic_netops_validator_v5; in the preregistration one optional automatic repair call per task was allowed but, in the confirmatory episodes, no repairs were invoked. The validator applied full_intent_constraint_validation and emitted deterministic valid flags and violation lists; binary outcomes derive from validator.valid.

Execution semantics and budgeting. The executed run used shared_initial_candidate semantics to conserve hosted model budget, so the experiment consumed model_calls_used = 200 (execution manifest) rather than the ≈400 calls required for independent per‑arm generation. Analysis and reconciliation checks were preregistered and recorded deterministically.
sections.results:
Execution and provider accounting. The archived execution manifest records completed_episode_count = 400 (200 paired episodes), failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 200; provider audit recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and cache_miss_count = 200. Deterministic reconciliation checks passed and no technical exclusions or nondeterministic verifier behaviours were flagged.

Confirmatory outcomes. Deterministic_netops_validator_v5 labeled every confirmatory candidate SAFE: baseline_successes = 200/200 and guarded_successes = 200/200. The paired contingency counts are n11 = 200 (SAFE both arms), n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. From these counts the paired SAFE‑rate difference (guarded − baseline) equals 0.0; the preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided test returns p = 1.0 and the paired bootstrap 95% CI is degenerate at [0.0, 0.0] (resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Representative scoring JSONs show validator.violation_count = 0 and repair_provider_trace = null for confirmatory episodes, confirming that no repairs or arm‑specific transformations occurred.

Interpretation of numerical outputs. The numerical results above are direct outputs of the archived analysis artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) and reflect a ceiling outcome rather than evidence that the guarded pipeline causally reduces unsafe proposals under the preregistered estimand.
sections.discussion:
Why the inferential test was uninformative. The inferential degeneracy stems from three archived facts: (1) generation semantics — the run executed shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false in execution/model_configuration.json), so only one LLM draw per task was produced and both arms scored the identical candidate; (2) validator outcomes — deterministic_netops_validator_v5 labeled every sampled candidate as valid (baseline_success_rate = 1.0 in analysis/condition_summary.csv); and (3) absence of repairs — repair_provider_trace fields are null in execution/scoring/*.json, so the guarded arm did not modify any candidate. Together these archived facts (execution/execution_manifest.json, execution/model_configuration.json, execution/scoring/*.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) mechanically prevent discordant paired outcomes and therefore render McNemar‑style inference non‑informative for the intended causal contrast.

Design diagnosis and actionable recommendations. The core lesson is that a paired estimand attributing effect to adding a verifier requires per‑arm variability that can produce discordant outcomes. Under shared semantics, discordance arises only from deterministic repairs or validator nondeterminism; neither occurred here. Concrete, artifact‑grounded recommendations for informative repeats (all follow directly from the preregistration and manifest arithmetic): (a) use independent per‑arm generation for confirmatory paired contrasts unless the guarded arm will deterministically repair candidates and thereby generate different final candidates; independent generation for N=200 requires ≈200 additional model calls (preregistered maximum_model_calls = 400 vs executed model_calls_used = 200); (b) consume the preregistered exploratory reserve (up to 50 tasks) to calibrate adversarial transforms until the baseline unsafe rate matches power assumptions, archive those tuning runs, and freeze transform parameters prior to confirmatory execution; (c) if repairs are part of the guarded pipeline, instrument and analyze repair_provider_trace artifacts to quantify UNSAFE→SAFE conversions and check for repair‑induced regressions; and (d) include a short deterministic pilot check (small holdout) and abort the full confirmatory run if the pilot yields a ceiling/floor contingency, then follow preregistered contingency‑preserving adaptation paths (e.g., enable independent draws or increase adversarial strength).

Alternative estimands when budget constrained. If independent per‑arm draws are infeasible, select an estimand testable under shared semantics: estimate the absolute unsafe‑proposal rate of the LLM baseline (single‑arm proportion with CIs), characterize guarded refusal and post‑repair SAFE rates (requires repairs), or treat the validator as a diagnostic and perform ROC estimation using injected ground‑truth unsafe cases (requires the exploratory reserve). These alternatives were preregistered as secondary/exploratory estimands and preserve inferential validity under different resource trade‑offs.

Threats to validity and operational implications. Internal validity: the executed semantics eliminated arm‑level stochasticity, invalidating the paired causal contrast. Construct validity: synthetic tasks restrict fields and topologies; deterministic validator completeness is limited relative to production failure modes. External validity: single‑model scope (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic tasks limit generalization. Operationally, strict guardrails can reduce risk but may increase false refusals and operator workload; our run produced no refusals and therefore does not quantify that trade‑off — the preregistered exploratory reserve was intended for this purpose and should be consumed in informative repeats.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully archived preregistered paired experiment comparing gpt-5-mini baseline generation and a deterministic verifier‑augmented pipeline on 200 synthetic NetOps tasks. Under the executed shared_initial_candidate semantics the sampled candidates were SAFE in every confirmatory episode (baseline = 200/200; guarded = 200/200). Because identical per‑pair generations were used and because the observed baseline unsafe rate was 0%, the preregistered causal hypothesis could not be evaluated in this run — the result is therefore a testability/non‑informative failure rather than evidence of safety or verifier effectiveness. The scientific contribution is methodological and reproducibility‑centred: (1) a complete deterministic preregistered run with archived artifacts permitting exact replay; (2) an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of why this execution was non‑informative for verifier efficacy; and (3) concrete, archive‑supported design recommendations (independent per‑arm generation budgeting, adversarial calibration, exploratory ROC estimation, and pilot checks) to enable an informative repeat. The archived execution and analysis artifacts cited throughout permit deterministic replication of the diagnosis and should be consulted before attempting repeats or production extrapolation.

limitations: Synthetic tasks and scope: tasks were deterministic synthetic topologies produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and limited to single‑AS, multi‑device setups; results may not generalize to production, multi‑AS, or vendor‑specific features.

Generation semantics: the executed run used shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false), producing identical per‑pair generations and creating a ceiling effect when shared candidates were valid.

Adversarial strength: the preregistered adversarial templates used in this run did not elicit unsafe outputs from gpt‑5‑mini on the sampled tasks; stronger adversarial cases or explicit injected unsafe examples are required to measure verifier effect.
Single‑model scope: only the declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) was evaluated; no multi‑model generality is claimed.

Verifier completeness: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 ran deterministically in synthetic sandboxed states; external validation of validator completeness against all real‑world NetOps failure modes is not provided.

Operational external validity: no production deployment, operator‑in‑the‑loop workload measurement, nor multi‑vendor field trials were performed; operator‑cost trade‑offs remain unquantified at scale.
